LUXVAR

A constructed symbolic language

LUXVAR is a constructed language (a "conlang," in the tradition of Esperanto, Klingon, or Tolkien's Elvish languages) created by Reza Nirouyar as part of the VARZIN project. Its broader design layer lists 801 entries across five intended thematic axes — Light, Reflection, Silence, Gate, and Motion. Core-30 is the public registry subset used in several tests; 801 is not a count of equally validated roots.

Project computational studies reported distinctive phonotactic and morphemic patterns under specified comparison corpora and procedures. Historical Claude/Gemini clustering agreement was reported as ARI 0.812, a qualified surface/morpheme result whose raw pairwise scoring was not independently reverified at correction; it does not measure intended semantic-axis recovery. Later frozen tests were near chance under their protocols. Separate explicitly trained interventions recovered targeted labels or group position, while systematic held-out composition was not demonstrated in the tested Appendix G procedure.

These structural findings are documented in the project's research record. What has not been established: that LUXVAR connects to any external field, that its words carry frequency-based meaning, or that its structure reflects anything beyond intentional linguistic design. LUXVAR is presented here as a work of constructed-language art, not as a scientific instrument.

Design layer: 801 entries; Core-30 public subset

Axes: 5 (Light, Reflection, Silence, Gate, Motion)

Creator: Reza Nirouyar

Full record: Cyclical Resonance report
